title: Cang Yutian's Weakness
next_chapter_hook: The moment Chen Ji's fingertips touched the chessboard, a fleeting wave—something even Cang Yutian himself had not noticed—flashed through those eyes that had remained unchanged for millennia. It was a longing sealed away for countless ages.

text.content: The transmission in the Mental Sea was like thunder, and Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Han Lie's arrogant face surfaced in his mind, accompanied by the threat: 'If you don't concede within three breaths, I'll cripple one of her meridians first.' Yet in this fleeting moment, another voice—ancient and weary—arose from the depths of his Mental Sea. It was the Scribe of Fate, an existence that had not spoken for thirty thousand years, now exhausting its final strength to deliver information that could reverse the heavens. 'Cang Yutian's core weakness...' The Scribe of Fate's voice was like a dying candle in the wind. 'Is that he has never possessed a true emotional bond.'

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji, this One is quite curious.' Cang Yutian sat behind the Heavenly Dao Chessboard, and a rare hint of amusement appeared in those eyes that surveyed all living beings. 'You know that Han Lie has already captured Chen Nian, yet you remain so composed. Are you relying on some hidden advantage, or—' He paused. 'Are you waiting for some variable?'

text.content: The Scribe of Fate's voice continued echoing in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, this time bringing forth an image sealed away for countless ages—a scene of Cang Yutian before he became the Eye of Heavenly Dao, kneeling before a solitary grave. In that grave lay the only bond he had ever known: his master. In that vision, the young Cang Yutian displayed human sadness for the first time, and that very sadness was brutally erased after he became the Eye of Heavenly Dao. 'This is his fatal flaw.' The Scribe of Fate sighed. 'Throughout his ancient scheme, he lacks nothing—except the emotion that would make him 'human'.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji raised his head, a meaningful smile curving his lips. He stared directly into Cang Yutian's eyes that seemed capable of seeing through everything and calmly spoke: 'Cang Yutian, you have schemed for countless ages, calculating all beings under heaven, but have you ever calculated one question—' His voice was not loud, yet it clearly spread throughout the entire Heavenly Dao Chessboard space. 'In this life of yours, have you ever had a true friend?'

text.content: This sentence was like an invisible blade, piercing straight into Cang Yutian's unchanging mask of cold indifference. The air seemed to freeze in that moment. Chen Ji clearly saw that Cang Yutian's fingers, gripping the chess piece, paused slightly—that was an extremely subtle movement, so subtle that if Chen Ji had not used the Tianji Record to peer into the deepest loneliness of his heart, it would have been impossible to detect. 'He is shaken.' Chen Ji silently recited in his heart. 'The invincible Eye of Heavenly Dao for countless ages, yet before the word 'friend,' he showed a trace of wavering.'

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian fell silent for a moment, then emitted a low, cold laugh. 'Friend?' His voice carried the mockery of ten thousand years of ice. 'This One transcends the cycle of reincarnation, gazing down upon all living beings—what need has This One for friends? Those bonds of emotion as insignificant as ants are nothing but stumbling blocks on the path of cultivation.' Yet as he spoke these words, his gaze unconsciously drifted toward a certain direction of emptiness—that was the direction of the solitary grave, where his memories sealed for countless ages resided.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji must make a choice: how to exploit this slight emotional flaw in Cang Yutian?

choices.text: Using Chen Nian as an Emotional Variable
choices.description: Exploiting the sister's special nature as 'Heavenly Fate Lock-Key,' revealing her fate entanglement with Cang Yutian, and using familial bonds to shake his Dao Heart.
choices.visible_reward: The First Crack Appears in Cang Yutian's Dao Heart
choices.risk_hint: Chen Nian's Safety Cannot Be Guaranteed

text.content: Chen Ji slowly opened his mouth: 'Cang Yutian, do you know why Chen Nian can interfere with the Tianji Record's foresight? Because she is—' He deliberately paused, his burning gaze fixed intently on Cang Yutian. 'The seed you personally planted in ancient times, the 'Heavenly Fate Lock-Key' that has yet to sprout.'

choices.text: Using Su Qingyao as an Emotional Variable
choices.description: Awakening Su Qingyao's feelings for Chen Ji, letting Cang Yutian witness a bond of 'protection' that he cannot comprehend, thereby impacting his perception.
choices.visible_cost: Expose the Relationship with Su Qingyao
choices.visible_reward: Cang Yutian Experiences His First Confusion Over 'Bonds'
choices.risk_hint: May Put Su Qingyao in Greater Danger

text.content: Chen Ji smiled lightly, turning to gaze in the direction where Su Qingyao was located: 'You ask me why I am unafraid? Because there is someone willing to die for me.' His voice was calm, yet carried undeniable certainty. 'And you, Cang Yutian—throughout your countless ages, has there ever been one person willing to do this for you?'

choices.text: Using One's Own Emotions as the Variable
choices.description: Openly confessing to Cang Yutian Chen Ji's true feelings toward Chen Nian, Su Qingyao, and every person in this chaotic world, using genuine emotion to break through his coldness.
choices.visible_reward: The Scribe of Fate Approves, Revealing the Ultimate Secret of the Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: Cang Yutian might exploit Chen Ji's emotions

text.content: Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, and when he opened them again, that always-cold gaze unexpectedly showed a rare warmth. 'I am indeed scheming,' he admitted, 'but my schemes are never for the world, but for—' He paused. 'To let the people I care about live well. This is what you can never understand, Cang Yutian.'

As Chen Ji's words fell, the entire Heavenly Dao Chessboard space fell into an eerie silence. In Cang Yutian's eyes, unchanging for ten thousand years, a rare confusion flickered—the emotion an ancient powerhouse had never experienced. He slowly spoke, his voice carrying a tremor he himself had not noticed: 'For the people one cares about...' He chewed on these words, as if tasting a delicacy he had never tried before. 'This feeling... this subordinate truly have never possessed.'
Chen Ji敏锐地捕捉到了仓御天话语中的那一丝裂痕。命运书写者说得没错——这个布局万古、将天下苍生视为棋子的天道之眼，内心深处最渴望的，恰恰是他亲手抛弃的那份人类情感。「你想试试吗？」陈机忽然开口，嘴角勾起一抹meaningful的笑容，「我可以让你体验一下，拥有'在乎的人'是什么感觉。」

choice.prompt: Chen Ji is probing Cang Yutian's bottom line and needs to decide the next strategy:

choices.description: Continue to verbally stimulate Cang Yutian, intensify the attack while his Dao heart is unstable, giving him no chance to breathe.
choices.visible_reward: Cang Yutian's emotions become further uncontrollabl
choices.risk_hint: Excessive words may cause the situation to lose control

text.content: Chen Ji pressed on relentlessly: 'For ten thousand years, you've stood high above, gazing down at all living beings, yet you don't even have a single person willing to collect your remains. Isn't that pitiful?' His voice was like a blade, every word heartpiercing. A crack finally appeared on Cang Yutian's face—that was the first crack in the ancient Dao heart.

choices.text: Retreat to advance, throw out bait
choices.description: Deliberately show weakness, express willingness to submit, in exchange for Cang Yutian's favor, laying the groundwork for a comeback.
choices.visible_cost: May be despised by Cang Yutian

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly sheathed his edge, slightly bowing: 'The junior has learned much. Perhaps... the junior should reconsider the relationship with the senior.' His posture was extremely low, but a subtle gleam flickered in his eyes—this was his specialty: playing dumb to eat the tiger.

Just then, the voice of the Destiny Chronicler sounded for the last time in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, this time with relief and joy: 'Child, you've found it. Cang Yutian's core weakness is his longing for emotions. And in your hands, you hold exactly what he has sought for ten thousand years—' The voice cut off abruptly, as if exhausted. But Chen Ji already understood: what he held was the possibility to shake Cang Yutian, his only chance to reverse this inevitable defeat.

dialogue.content: Cang Yutian slowly rose, his figure appearing infinitely tall in the void, yet revealing an indescribable loneliness. 'Chen Ji,' his voice was no longer the lofty judgment, but carried a near-human curiosity, 'you are interesting. In ten thousand years, you are the first to dare discuss 'emotions' with this subordinate.' He pointed at the chessboard, 'Continue. Whatever strategy you choose, this subordinate will accept.'

text.content: Chen Ji gazed at the intricate situation on the chessboard, his heart already set. Heavenly Fate was slowly draining away, but in exchange came a precious moment when an ancient power's Dao heart wavered. He thought of the Destiny Chronicler's testament letter—'Any prophetic vision with her in it is blurred'—that was Chen Nian, his sister, the starting point of his ten-thousand-year scheme, and now the key to leverage Cang Yutian's obsession. 'Sister...' he silently recited in his heart, 'This time, let brother save you.'

choice.prompt: At this critical moment, Chen Ji prepares to make his move. This hand will directly determine the direction of the chess game:

choices.text: Place the piece on the 'Emotion' position, striking the vital point
choices.description: Place the crucial piece on the chessboard, using Chen Nian's fate as the lure, completely tearing open Cang Yutian's emotional defense.
choices.visible_cost: Chen Nian falls into greater danger
choices.visible_reward: Cang Yutian's Dao heart collapses, chess game reverses

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath and slowly placed the chess piece in the center of the board—the position no one had dared to place for ten thousand years, beside the Heavenly Origin, above the Life Gate. "This move, I place for my sister." His voice was calm as water. "Cang Yutian, do you dare accept?"

choices.text: Placing the 'Temptation' position, advancing step by step
choices.description: In the posture of a master strategist, advancing step by step to draw Cang Yutian into the game, subtly dismantling his mental defenses.

text.content: Chen Ji smiled faintly, his finger tracing across the board, leaving a meaningful trail: "Senior, there's no need to be impatient. This game, I wish to play slowly." His gaze was profound as an abyss. "After all, the game I intend to play extends far beyond this single board."

The moment the chess piece touched the board, the entire Heavenly Dao space trembled. Chen Ji sensed an unprecedented force surge from the board—that was destiny itself responding to his call. A complex light flickered in Cang Yutian's eyes—shock, confusion, and a trace of longing he himself had never noticed. "Interesting," the Ten-Thousand-Year Heavenly Dao Eye revealed its first genuine smile, "For ten thousand years, the first piece that makes this seat feel 'anticipation.'"

Just as Chen Ji placed his piece, Han Lie, far away somewhere, suddenly felt an inexplicable chill. He looked down at the imprisoned Chen Nian in his hands, only to find this woman's lips curved into a smile completely contrary to his expectations—mockery, disdain, and an absolute trust. "What's going on?" Han Lie frowned. Chen Nian didn't answer, only murmuring to herself: "Brother found it... he found the weakness of that invincible being through the ages." Her voice grew softer, yet more certain, "Cang Yutian, you have lost."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji withdrew his finger from the board, his gaze toward Cang Yutian carrying a deeper, meaning-laden quality: "Senior, what have you pursued for ten thousand years? To transcend the Heavenly Dao and become the true 'Dao' itself. But have you ever considered—" he paused slightly, "when a person has lost even 'emotion,' what meaning is there in becoming the 'Dao'?"

text.content: These words struck like a heavy hammer against Cang Yutian's unchanging Dao heart that had remained steady for ten thousand years. He fell silent, more silent than ever before. In those eyes that gazed down upon all living beings, true bewilderment appeared for the first time—the confusion of an existence that had lived for ten thousand years, questioning for the first time the "Dao" it pursued. "Chen Ji," he finally spoke, his voice carrying a near-human weariness, "you have won this round." After a pause, he continued: "But in the next round, this seat will not give you another chance."

Upon hearing this, Chen Ji's smile deepened. He knew Cang Yutian was right—this was merely victory in the first round, and the true game had just begun. But he had already found the fulcrum to pry open the ten-thousand-year chess game, discovered the key to causing that lofty Heavenly Dao Eye to waver. "Senior," Chen Ji stood up, his gaze blazing like fire, "I told you, the game I intend to play extends far beyond this single board." He turned, his robes fluttering: "Next time, I will make you truly understand—what is 'emotion.'"

Just as Chen Ji turned, he perceived a faint fluctuation in his Mental Sea—that was the last trace of consciousness from the Fate Scribe, carrying relief and expectation. "Child," that voice was like a candle flame in the wind, "you did it. Cang Yutian's Dao heart has begun to crack... but remember, this is only the beginning. His obsession runs too deep, and the cracks may heal at any moment." Chen Ji nodded silently, carving this warning into his heart. Outside the window, the horizon was already brightening with the first light of dawn, and his game against Cang Yutian had only just begun.
